jobs.prompt: Rework the S9 Cluster change order that is already in docs/scope/roadmap.md and docs/architecture/cluster.md (read both first). Problems: (A) it renumbered the existing owner-provided requirements R-050 (rented GPU worker bursts) and R-051 (cloud CPU runners) to R-062 and R-063: restore them to R-050 and R-051 exactly as in the original text (git show HEAD~1:docs/scope/roadmap.md has it), unchanged in every word. (B) Re-number and reorder the S9 section so the cluster requirements are R-052 to R-065, in the owner priority order below, each written in the existing style (heading sentence, Acceptance list of 3 to 5 checkable lines). The owner priority order, which is also the build order: R-052 One shared ledger with ticket leases replaces hand-off branches and ticket ID ranges (claim with lease, heartbeat, automatic expiry, fencing token, zero double builds, a dead node tickets return to the pool). R-053 Coordination events (ticket-done, release-shipped, lease claim and release, request, question, handoff, ack) are typed swarm-to-swarm messages that use no model turns and no orchestrator tokens, and an orchestrator is woken only for a decision (acceptance: a ticket-done from node B reaches node A and updates the ledger with 0 model calls; the wake event fires only for kinds that need a decision). R-054 Reliable delivery: acks, bounded retries with backoff, a durable outbox on disk, de-duplication, and catch-up after a node sleeps or reconnects (acceptance: 1000 messages queued while a node is offline are delivered in order exactly once after it returns; a message is never lost on crash of sender or receiver). R-055 Any machine joins with swarm join using tailnet auth and registers in the node registry with capabilities (cores, RAM, lanes, GPU, machine limit) and live capacity (real memory pressure and swap, free slots, lane health; use the real free-memory reading, not the Node os.freemem value, which undercounts on macOS by about 30 times). R-056 Typed signed messages: per-node keys, schema validation, never executable, secret scan on send and on receive, replay protection, forged-sender rejection, tailnet only. R-057 Autonomous node flows never perform owner-only actions: approve, merge to live, deploy, caps, spend and keys stay owner-only on every node; a message that tries is dropped, logged and raised to the owner. R-058 A release-ready event makes the other nodes run swarm update between waves, never mid-wave, respecting pinned projects and the when-idle rule. R-059 One repo-wide merge queue across nodes: PRs from any node merge in one order through swarm merge, with the green-check requirement, one at a time, no node merges around the queue. R-060 Placement and work stealing by real capacity: each node reports free slots, memory pressure and lanes; a node with free slots pulls ready tickets honoring file ownership, lane fit, ticket target worktree and fair share; heavy jobs go to the node with headroom. R-061 Messaging and nodes are visible: swarm msg send, list and tail, swarm node list, and the board shows the message log and node view for every machine. R-062 Release benchmarks per version against a fixed baseline stored under bench/cluster/ (event latency p50 and p95, ticket ready to started time, slot utilization, idle node-minutes while ready work exists, owner relays, double-claims, tickets per hour per node), the trend on Swarm Watch. R-063 CI fails when a benchmark regresses past its threshold (more than 10 percent worse throughput, more than 25 percent worse latency p95, more than 5 points worse utilization; any double-claim or owner relay above 0 fails) and the chaos tests (kill a node mid-ticket, drop the network, clock skew, two nodes claiming at once) pass. R-064 The MacBook and the Mac mini are the first two nodes and the relayed hand-off flow is retired once both run on the ledger. R-065 A third node joins and leaves without breaking leases, the queue or the board (three simulated nodes). Benchmark baseline: the Mac mini measured its own capacity on branch idle/cluster-measure-20261021/node-mini-measure (files docs/state/node-mini.md and bench/cluster/fixtures/node-mini.json, latency.json, claim-races.json, slot-use.json). Do not invent numbers from it (you cannot read it here): in cluster.md say the first baseline file bench/cluster/baseline.json is created from those fixtures by the C6 benchmark ticket, and that the measured facts to carry in are: 10 cores and 24 GB on the mini, os.freemem undercount of about 30 times, an average slot fill of 15 to 16 percent per project with a median of 1 job at a time, and an O_EXCL claim race with exactly one winner at 2, 8 and 32 contenders at 4 to 7 ms median (measured under a load average near 50, so pessimistic). Targets stay as already written (message latency p50 under 100 ms and p95 under 1 s; ready to started p95 under 30 s; utilization above 80 percent when work exists; idle node-minutes about 0; owner relays 0; double-claims 0). In cluster.md: update the stages C1 to C6 so the first wave is exactly items R-052 to R-054 (C1 ledger and leases, C2 typed events without model turns, C3 reliable delivery), then R-055 to R-057 (C4 nodes, signing, owner-only boundary), R-058 to R-060 (C5 updates, merge queue, placement), R-061 to R-065 (C6 board, benchmarks, chaos, cutover); fix the requirements map table and every R number in the doc. Update tests/build-progress-roadmap.test.mjs expectations to the new total (51 original plus 14 = 65, with the comment) and run it and tests/build-progress-ledgers.test.mjs. Do not change any other existing requirement text. Keep cluster.md under 400 lines. No secrets, no real hosts or addresses.
